chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:
A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and asked him: 'O Abu Ja'far! Tell me about your Lord, when was He?'

He said: 'Woe be upon you! Verily, it is said to a thing that did not exist and then came into being: 'When was it?' Verily, my Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, has always been Ever-Living without a how (quality). There was no 'when' for Him, nor a 'how' for His existence, nor a 'where' for Him. He was not in a thing, nor on a thing. He did not create a place for His existence, nor was He strengthened after creating something, nor weak before creating something. He was not lonely before He originated something, nor does He resemble any created thing. He was not devoid of power over sovereignty before its creation, nor will He be devoid of it after its passing. He has always been Ever-Living without accidental life, and Sovereign, Powerful, before creating anything, and Sovereign, Compelling, after creating existence.'

So for His existence there is no 'how', no 'where' for Him, no limit, and He is not known by anything that resembles Him. He does not age due to long-lasting, nor is stunned by anything, nor does anything hollow Him out. All things become stunned from His fear. He is Ever-Living without a bare life or described existence, without a limited 'how', without a following effect, without a place that adjoined something. Rather, He is the Ever-Living Who is known, and the Sovereign who always has power and sovereignty. He created what He willed by His will. He is not limited, nor partial, nor perishing. He was the First without a 'how', and will be the Last without a 'where'. Everything is perishable except His Face. To Him belongs creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Woe be upon you, O questioner! Verily, my Lord is not covered by imaginations, nor do doubts descend upon Him. He is not joined by anything, nor does anything join Him. Incidents do not descend upon Him. He is not questioned about what He does. He does not fall upon anything. Slumber does not seize Him, nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the nature of Allah's existence in relation to time and space?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid exemplifies the Shia doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence) by systematically negating spatial and temporal categories (*kayf*, *ayn*, *hadd*) from Allah, distinguishing His eternal essence from created beings. Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that 'when' implies a beginning, whereas Allah's existence is uncaused and independent of the limitations of time and space, a key theological point in refuting anthropomorphism (*Tajsim*). The narration emphasizes that Allah's attributes are not accidental additions but are intrinsic to His eternal being, establishing the foundation for understanding divine unity (*Tawhid*) in Shia scholastic theology.
